title: Numbers in the Dots

patient.name: Master Daniel Goh Jun Wei
patient.presenting_complaint: New patient — referred for colour vision assessment after school screening flagged possible colour vision deficiency

history.hpc: Daniel's school conducted a routine vision and colour screening as part of the annual health check. He was flagged as having difficulty identifying certain colours during the school screening, particularly distinguishing red and green objects. His mother reports he sometimes confuses the colours of his crayons but otherwise has no visual complaints. He has been referred to SNEC for formal colour vision testing using the Ishihara chart.
history.pmhx: No previous eye surgery. No known ocular disease. Has never worn glasses.
history.family_hx: Maternal uncle is 'colour blind' (red-green colour vision deficiency)

iop.right: Not tested — not indicated for this visit
iop.left: Not tested — not indicated for this visit

ishihara_test.lighting_condition: Tested under natural daylight near a window, avoiding direct glare
ishihara_test.testing_distance: 75 cm from the chart, plates held perpendicular to line of sight
ishihara_test.right_eye_alone: Read 6 out of 17 plates correctly (with left eye occluded)
ishihara_test.left_eye_alone: Read 6 out of 17 plates correctly (with right eye occluded)
ishihara_test.pattern_of_errors: Consistently misread plates designed to detect red-green deficiency; correctly read the control/demonstration plate
ishihara_test.result: Pattern of plate readings consistent with a red-green colour vision deficiency, likely congenital given family history (maternal uncle)

investigations.va_distance: RE: 6/6. LE: 6/6 — visual acuity normal, colour vision deficiency does not affect VA

diagnosis: Ishihara colour vision testing completed for both eyes under appropriate lighting. Result pattern is consistent with a congenital red-green colour vision deficiency, correlating with the family history and school screening findings. For doctor's review and counselling.

immediate: Confirm patient identity and explain the test to Daniel and his mother in simple terms: 'finding the number hidden in the dots'
Ensure testing is conducted in good, even natural light, avoiding glare or dim lighting which can affect results
Hold the Ishihara plates at the correct distance (approximately 75 cm) and angle (perpendicular to the line of sight)
Show the demonstration/control plate first to confirm the patient understands the task
Test the right eye first with the left eye occluded, then the left eye with the right eye occluded — allow only a few seconds per plate
Record the number of plates read correctly out of the total presented for each eye
Note which specific plates were missed if possible, as the pattern of errors helps distinguish red-green from blue-yellow deficiencies
Document the testing conditions (lighting, distance) alongside the results, as these affect reliability
Hand results to doctor for review and discussion with the patient and parent
follow_up: Doctor to confirm the diagnosis and discuss implications with Daniel and his mother
Inform school of the result if relevant for accommodations (e.g. colour-coded learning materials)
No treatment is available for congenital colour vision deficiency, but counselling on practical adaptations can be offered
patient_education: Explain to Daniel and his mother that colour vision deficiency is usually inherited (often from the mother's side) and is not a disease of the eye itself
Reassure that his overall vision (6/6 in both eyes) is normal and this does not affect reading or most schoolwork
Advise that certain careers (e.g. some uniformed services, pilots) have colour vision requirements, which may be relevant for him to know in future, but this should be discussed with the doctor

key_points: Confirms patient identity and explains the test in age-appropriate language for a 12-year-old
Asks about family history of colour vision deficiency, which is relevant given the X-linked inheritance pattern
Confirms visual acuity is normal, establishing that any colour vision issue is isolated and not due to reduced VA
Notes the context: school screening flagged the issue, prompting referral
Ensures testing is performed under appropriate lighting (natural daylight, no glare) at the correct distance and angle
Uses the demonstration/control plate first to confirm the patient understands the task
Tests each eye separately with correct occlusion and allows only a brief time per plate
Documents the number of plates read correctly out of the total for each eye, and notes the pattern of errors if possible
Recognises that the Ishihara test screens for red-green colour vision deficiency
Identifies that the pattern of results (correct demonstration plate, consistent errors on red-green plates) suggests a congenital red-green deficiency
Does not make a definitive genetic or clinical diagnosis independently — refers to doctor
Correlates the family history (maternal uncle) with the likely inheritance pattern
Documents testing conditions (lighting, distance) and results (plates correct out of total, per eye) accurately
Hands results to doctor for review and family counselling
Provides reassurance and age-appropriate education to the child and parent about the nature of colour vision deficiency
Avoids causing unnecessary alarm while being honest about the finding
